notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Owner requested an implementation plan. Recorded K0-K9 in docs/backlog/notes/NOTE-20260913-knowledge-backlog-implementation/implementation-plan.md after inspecting Switcher 72452b5 and Hub 22afb65. Covers durable project identity and caller authorization, shared service/SQLite writes, web/MCP/CLI, memory/search, attachment backup/restore, loss-aware Hub import, per-project cutover and rollback, then playbooks and instruction composition. Includes test matrix, negative cases and acceptance gates. Technical choices are recommendations; planning only, no implementation or data migration. Feature remains open.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Owner requires SQLite to be easily replaceable by PostgreSQL. Recorded database-portability.md as a mandatory K1/K2 contract addendum: asynchronous persistence ports, engine-independent atomic operations and errors, shared adapter tests and logical data migration. Current synchronous stores do not yet satisfy this requirement; K0 acceptance did not establish PostgreSQL support.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Owner superseded the portability request: PostgreSQL is now the default and target database for porting LLM Ops Hub functionality into Switcher. Do not require a SQLite-first implementation or parallel new-feature adapters. Adapt K1/K2 and plan controlled migration of existing SQLite state. Drizzle remains a discussed implementation option, not an installed dependency.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Latest owner decision supersedes PostgreSQL-first: deliver the working Hub functionality on SQLite now and migrate to PostgreSQL later. SQLite and current synchronous persistence ports do not block K1 acceptance. Owner-session recovery and usable agent/token/grant management remain required; PostgreSQL, dual-engine tests and an ORM change are deferred.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Owner requested explicit slice-branch requirements. Added the branch/PR workflow to the implementation plan: one bounded slice per branch and PR to main, start subsequent slices from refreshed origin/main after the previous merge, declare branch/worktree/base SHA in worker handoffs, and require revision-bound checks before acceptance. Existing K0/K1 stays together on t3code/implement-llmopshub-worker-delegation; K2 starts on a new branch after merge. Canonical backlog decisions must be synchronized before handoff.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Owner clarified that t3code/implement-llmopshub-worker-delegation is the integration branch. This supersedes the preceding slice-to-main workflow: new slice branches start from the current integration branch after the preceding slice merges and target it by PR; the final integration PR targets main after acceptance of the agreed feature scope. Existing K0/K1 is already on integration and requires review of a fixed commit range and final SHA, without rewriting history or a self-PR. Further fixes use slice PRs; K2 starts after K0/K1 acceptance and required fixes merge. Canonical backlog stays on main, and slice acceptance does not close the parent feature.

problem: Useful conclusions and out-of-scope findings from human-agent conversations need a durable place where another human or model can discover, discuss, and continue them.
The current Git-backed Hub captures backlog plans but requires repository synchronization and an indirect human feedback flow. Switcher already provides related project and verification context.

risk.rollback: Introduce the module without migrating existing projects automatically. If the local trial fails, disable its entry points while retaining its database and a verified export; keep the original repository-backed backlog available until an explicit cutover.

scope: Use the linked plan as a phased umbrella; start with a bounded local thread/reply/search/task flow and split implementation slices before coding.
Reuse SQLite infrastructure and shared application services exposed through web/API, MCP, and CLI. Keep knowledge independent of server claims and worktree lifetime.
Preserve durable authorship, revision history, explicit decision provenance, retry safety, bounded reads, and linked evidence. Generate versioned Markdown/JSON snapshots when needed.
Plan a loss-aware import from LLM Ops Hub and one explicit write-location cutover per project. GitHub is not required for knowledge operations.
Keep the module able to run independently for optional future hosting. Accounts, remote access, tenant isolation, pricing, and hosted deployment remain later design work.

After the core workflow, add playbooks and report-only health monitoring, repository instruction inspection, then AGENTS.md assembly from explicitly approved scoped rules. Preserve per-document repository-owned versus service-generated source-of-truth boundaries; see delivery phases 4-6.
title: Add shared project memory, discussions, and backlog for humans and agents
validation: A human and two agent sessions save a discussion, reply, find it, and create a linked task without starting or claiming a managed server.
Fixtures verify restart persistence, duplicate-request handling, conflicting edits, project access boundaries, superseded knowledge, and export provenance.
Removing a worktree or pruning runtime logs does not delete knowledge; explicit knowledge backup and restore preserve linked records.
Import fixtures preserve legacy IDs, source authorship labels, dates, relationships, and attachments; unsupported data is reported and repeated imports are safe.
Record actual owner workflow usefulness and retrieval effort before expanding scope or making efficiency or business claims.

Playbook checks advance with time and expose unavailable/stale evidence; instruction fixtures cover scope, provenance, dirty sources, approved-only generation, stale bases, and manual drift without implicit command execution or repository writes.
value: The owner can ask an agent to save a conversation outcome once and have humans and other models continue from the same durable context.
A reusable open-source module can later support optional managed hosting without giving the host control over customer development processes.
